newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Afghan Taleban stage anti-foreign protest.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban stage anti-foreign protest.

text.p: Kabul's Taleban rulers gathered about 500 civil servants and residents to stage a protest against what they called foreign interference by neighbours on Thursday.

The protesters, who marched more than one mile (km) through the city centre to the Iranian embassy and the U.N. political office in Kabul, slammed Russia, Iran and India as the main culprits. "Death to interventionists! Down with Iran and Russia!" chanted a Taleban preacher, standing on a car roof, through a megaphone.

It was the first such demonstration under the Taleban administration in Kabul, and was clearly staged with its blessing. Armed Taleban fighters guarded the procession and were often the only ones shouting slogans through most of the march.

Very few of the other marchers seemed enthusiastic or echoed the slogans. Among them was a group of 30 women and children, one of whom said that the Taleban movement should lift its restrictions on work and education for women.
"We ask the Taleban to provide education and job opportunities for women of Afghanistan," said the burkha-clad woman, who taught for 40 years in Kabul until the Taleban takeover last month.
Some said they had been summoned for a morning meeting and then had been told to join the march. "It is like a spontaneous demonstration. We didn't know anything about it," one participant said.
